# Glossary

The terms the CLI, the application and the MCP server use. The Glossary view of the application shows the same entries; both are made from one source.

## Basics

### Measured and estimated

A measured value was read from the client's own data, for example the token counts of a response. An estimated value was computed from file sizes, heuristics or the price table and is marked with a tilde (~) and the warning color. “n/a” means the client does not record the value at all.

### Session

A session is one conversation with a client such as Claude Code, OpenCode, Copilot CLI or VS Code Copilot. Session time runs from the first to the last event, so idle time is included.

### Request

Every time the client sends the conversation to the model, that is one request. Everything in the static context is sent again with each one, which is why small items add up.

### Tokens

Tokens are the unit in which models read input and write output, and in which usage is billed. Where the client reports no count, AgentLens estimates tokens from the size of the content.

### Source

A source is one supported client: Claude Code, OpenCode, Copilot CLI or VS Code Copilot. Use the source filter at the top to include or exclude them.

### Subagent

Subagents work in their own context. Their requests are counted separately from the main agent's, which is why context size only covers main-agent requests.

## Context

### Static context

Tool definitions, instruction files (such as CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md), agent and skill listings and MCP server instructions. The client sends them with every request, so they cost tokens whether they are used or not.

### Context size

The number of tokens the model received for one request (uncached input plus cache reads and writes). It is measured and only counted for main-agent requests. It grows over a session until the client compacts it.

### Overhead

A 500-token instruction file that was sent with 200 requests caused 100,000 tokens of overhead. Overhead shows which static content is expensive because it is large, because it is sent often, or both. It is an estimate. For skills it is baseline + load + carry.

### Owner

The file, plugin, MCP server or built-in that provides the item. Group by project to see which project adds how much.

### Kind

Tool listing and tool definition: the tools the model may call. MCP instructions: text an MCP server adds. Instruction file: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and similar. Agent listing and skill listing: names and descriptions of installed agents and skills.

### First request

Its size is measured, so it is an upper bound of all static context a session starts with.

### Idle cost

What an installed skill, agent or MCP server costs while it does nothing. “Unknown” means the client reports no data for MCP servers.

## Skills

### Baseline

Clients list installed skills by name and description in each request so the model knows they exist. That is the baseline: the cost of having the skill installed, even if it is never used.

### Load

When a skill is invoked, its full instructions enter the context once. Load is the size of that content.

### File use

A skill is not only loaded by the client's skill tool or by typing its name: a model also reads its files and runs the scripts in its folder. AgentLens counts those tool calls per installed skill (only the skill name is kept, never the command or the path), and a skill with file uses is not listed as unused. Looking after a skill does not count: listing, printing, copying or committing its files, and editing them, and neither do the file accesses of a session that edits the skill. It is a signal, not proof. Loads are shown in the uses column; file uses are listed next to them.

### Carry

Once loaded, the skill text stays in the conversation and is re-sent with every following request until a compaction removes it. Carry is that repeated cost and always an estimate.

### Attributed

Only available from clients that report it (OpenTelemetry). Measured.

### Follow-on

An assumption: everything that happens until something else takes over is attributed to the skill. Use it as a rough guide, not as a measurement.

## Cost

### Cost

Reported cost is shown as is. Otherwise the tokens are priced with the price table. Cache writes are priced as 5-minute writes. Add prices for unknown models to ~/.config/agentlens/prices.json.

### Premium requests

Copilot counts requests against a monthly allowance instead of billing tokens. They are shown next to the cost, never added to it.

### Unpriced

They are left out of totals and shares instead of being counted as free.

### What if

Shows what the period would have cost on a different model. “Excluded” requests have no actual price and are left out of both sides.

### Impact

Every advice finding has an impact: its saving in tokens, the saving in USD (always an estimate, computed from the price table) and the confidence of the saving. The findings are ranked by it: by the USD saving, without any price by the tokens weighted by class (input 1, cache write 1.25, cache read 0.1); findings without a saving come last.

### Saving

For unused skills and costly descriptions the listing tokens that removing or shortening would have saved; for large skill bodies the body above 2,000 tokens times the requests that carried it; for MCP servers their context where none of their tools was called; for the context size the input above each session's first request on requests of at least 200,000 tokens. Findings that know their requests price each with its own model, the others with the period's average price per token class.

### Confidence

Measured: every number behind the saving came from the client. Estimated: some were computed from file sizes or heuristics. Inferred: the saving rests on an assumption about how the work could have run instead, for example that it could have started in a fresh session.

## Efficiency

### Cache read

Repeated prefixes of a conversation are cached by the provider. Reading from the cache is much cheaper and faster than sending new input.

### Cache write

The first time content is sent it is written to the cache. Later requests can read it.

### Hit rate

Measured. “n/a” means the client reports no cache tokens.

## Flow

### Peak

Measured over the main agent's requests.

### Near limit

Of the model's documented window, or, if the window does not fit the data, of the largest size at which that model was compacted.

### Compaction

After a compaction, content that was carried along (such as loaded skills) is gone from the context.

### Retry loop

Calls without a recorded outcome are “unknown” and never counted as errors.

### Permission wait

It includes the time the user was away from the keyboard.
